Main.sentence: Sidley Austin LLP is an American ___E:multinational U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multinational_corporation)___ ___E:law firm U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Law_firm)___ with approximately 2,300 lawyers in 21 offices across the world, including North America, Europe, Asia, and Australia.

It was established in 1866 and its headquarters is at ___E:One South Dearborn U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/One_South_Dearborn)___ in ___E:Chicago U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago)___ 's ___E:Loop U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_Loop)___ .
It is ___E:one of the largest law firms in the world in terms of revenue U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_largest_law_firms_by_revenue)___ .
In 1866, Norman Williams and John L. Thompson founded the law firm of Williams & Thompson in Chicago, Illinois.

In 1876, the firm organized the ___E:Western Electric Company U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_Electric)___ and ___E:Illinois Bell U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Illinois_Bell)___ , and the ___E:Bell System U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bell_System)___ became a longtime client.  ___E:Mary Todd Lincoln U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mary_Todd_Lincoln)___ was another early client,  seeking counsel following her husband ___E:Abraham Lincoln's death U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Assassination_of_Abraham_Lincoln)___ .
William Pratt Sidley, who had joined the firm in 1892, was added to the firm's name in 1900 when it was renamed Holt, Wheeler & Sidley.

Edwin C. Austin joined the firm in 1914.  Among the firm's first clients were the ___E:Pullman Company U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pullman_Company)___ , the manufacturer of specialty sleeping railway cars, as well as ___E:Western Electric U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_Electric)___ and ___E:Illinois Steel U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Illinois_Steel)___ .

In 1963, former postmaster general ___E:J. Edward Day U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/J._Edward_Day)___ left the administration of ___E:President John F. Kennedy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy)___ to establish the firm's ___E:Washington, D.C. U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington,_D.C.)___ office.
Initial clients included the Advertising Mail Marketing Association.
In 1972, Sidley & Austin, with 100 lawyers, merged with the 50 lawyers of Chicago firm Leibman, Williams, Bennett, Baird & Minow.

Additional offices were then established in London in 1974 and in Singapore and New York in 1982.  Day, a chair of the firm's Washington, D.C., office prior to the merger, sued Sidley & Austin in response to the relocation of the merged firm's Washington office and being asked to share chairmanship of the office, although Day had approved and signed the merger agreement and amended partner agreement.
A U.S.
District Court judge dismissed the suit, and all appeals were denied.
The case is sometimes cited in discussions of partnership law.
In 1975, Charles E. Lomax joined the firm, later becoming its first black partner.
His clients included ___E:Don King U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_King)___ and ___E:Muhammad Ali U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muhammad_Ali)___ ,  for whom the firm arranged fights.
In the late 1970s and early 1980s, Sidley & Austin represented AT&T in the time leading up to and during United States v. AT&T .
In 1985, Sidley & Austin became the first law firm to establish a standalone appellate practice for U.S.

Supreme Court cases,  recruiting ___E:Benjamin W. Heineman Jr. U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benjamin_W._Heineman_Jr.)___ to lead it, as well as former ___E:U.S. Solicitor General U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Solicitor_General)___ ___E:Rex E. Lee U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rex_E._Lee)___ .

By 2012, the firm had argued 106 Supreme Court cases and was involved in approximately 40% of the cases the Court heard each year. The head of Sidley's D.C. office, Carter Phillips,  had argued 76 cases before the Supreme Court by June 2012, more than any other active lawyer.

Sidley & Austin was among several law firms involved in the ___E:Savings & Loan Crisis U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Savings_%26_Loan_Crisis)___ ; the firm paid $7.5 million in 1991 to settle ___E:legal malpractice U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legal_malpractice)___ claims stemming from its representation of the ___E:Lincoln Savings and Loan Association U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lincoln_Savings_and_Loan_Association)___ .

Michelle Obama (formerly Robinson) met her future husband and future President Barack Obama in 1989 while both worked at Sidley, when Michelle was in her first year as an associate and Barack was a summer associate.
In 1995, a group of women lawyers at Sidley co-founded the firm's Women in Leadership program.

In 2001, the firm merged with ___E:Brown & Wood U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brown_%26_Wood)___ , a New York-based law firm established in 1914 with 400 attorneys and additional domestic offices in Washington, D.C., San Francisco and Los Angeles and overseas branches in London, Beijing and Hong Kong (where it practiced English law in addition to U.S. law).

Brown & Wood was known for its ___E:securities U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Securities)___ , ___E:structured finance U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Structured_finance)___ and ___E:securitization U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Securitization)___ practices.
Brown & Wood had offices in the ___E:World Trade Center U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Trade_Center_(1973%E2%80%932001))___ on floors 54 and 56-59.

The combined firm planned to move into the World Trade Center; it was decorating and furnishing additional space when the ___E:September 11 attacks U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/September_11_attacks)___ occurred.

In July 2002, Sidley Austin moved into the ___E:Axa Equitable Center U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Axa_Equitable_Center)___ in ___E:Midtown Manhattan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Midtown_Manhattan)___ .
In 2002, Sidley was among the first law firms to establish a practice dedicated to ___E:international trade law U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_trade_law)___ .
The firm signed on as the anchor tenant for ___E:One South Dearborn U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/One_South_Dearborn)___ in Chicago in 2003.

In 2007, Sidley Austin agreed to pay $39 million as part of a settlement with the ___E:Internal Revenue Service U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Internal_Revenue_Service)___ , which allowed the firm to avoid criminal charges of alleged fraudulent tax shelter activities.
The previous year, Sidley and KPMG agreed to pay $54 million to investors who bought the shelters.

Sidley Austin represented ___E:Airbus U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Airbus)___ in petitioning the ___E:World Trade Organization U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Trade_Organization)___ to allow the European Union to take countermeasures against the U.S. government in response to its subsidies of ___E:Boeing U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boeing)___ , succeeding in 2019.  As of 2019, the firm had represented a party in approximately half of the last 550 disputes brought before the World Trade Organization.
Sidley maintains offices in 21 cities worldwide,  adding ___E:Miami U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miami)___ in 2022  and ___E:San Diego U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Diego)___ in 2024.

In August 2019, Politico reported that the Chinese technology company, ___E:Huawei U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Huawei)___ , hired Sidley Austin to lobby on their behalf after the ___E:Trump administration U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trump_administration)___ set restrictions on their business transactions with the U.S.
Federal Government.
Trade, sanctions, export controls, "and other national security-related topics," were to be the subjects of lobbying efforts, according to reported disclosure filings.

In October of 2022, Reuters and Politico reported that Sidley Austin updated its registration under the ___E:Foreign Agents Registration Act U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foreign_Agents_Registration_Act)___ as a lobbyist for ___E:Hikvision USA U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hikvision)___ , a California-based subsidiary of the Chinese video surveillance company, as requested by the ___E:U.S. Justice Department U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Department_of_Justice)___ .

In their registration, the law firm reported having received approximately $7.4 million in fees since beginning their representation in 2018. The firm had initially registered under the ___E:U.S. Lobbying Disclosure Act U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lobbying_Disclosure_Act_of_1995)___ when it was first retained by the company.
Sidley Austin was hired by ___E:DJI Technologies U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DJI)___ in early 2024 after the drone maker was dropped by other agencies in February of that year.
Sidley Austin is the sixth-largest law firm in the world by revenue in 2025, according to The American Lawyer .
The firm has approximately 2,300 lawyers  and annual revenue over $3.4 billion.
The firm is one of the highest-paying companies in the U.S.

In 2023, BTI Consulting Group named Sidley to its Client Service A-Team  – one of three law firms to appear in every edition of the ranking since its inception in 2001.  Other honors include the American Bar Association's 2019 Champions for Disability Inclusion in the Legal Profession Award.  and being named a 2019 "Litigation Department of the Year" finalist by The American Lawyer .
The group was named a 2019 International Trade Group of the Year by Law360  and has been honored as "Law Firm of the Year" in Trade & Customs by Who's Who Legal for 15 consecutive years.

Its appellate and ___E:US Supreme Court U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/US_Supreme_Court#blank)___ practice has been featured in ___E:USA Today U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USA_Today#blank)___ , ___E:BusinessWeek U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BusinessWeek#blank)___ , the ___E:American Lawyer U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Lawyer#blank)___ , the ___E:Legal Times U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legal_Times#blank)___ , and the ___E:National Law Journal U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Law_Journal#blank)___ . ___E: U:(https://en.wikipedia.org#_blank)___
In 2020, Sidley was named "Firm of the Year" in Capital Markets (Overseas); Corporate Compliance; Healthcare, Pharma and Life Sciences; and Real Estate and REIT by China Business Law Journal.
In 2018, Sidley was named Competition & Regulatory Team of the Year at The Lawyer Awards in London.
In 2024, Sidley has been named a “Firm of the Year” in six categories at the China Business Law Awards 2024  .

Sidley Austin partner George Fatheree worked ___E:pro bono U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pro_bono)___ on behalf of the descendants of Willa and Charles Bruce  to execute the return of beachfront land which had been seized by Los Angeles authorities in the 1920s.
The couple had lost the property, known as Bruce's Beach, when the state claimed it for public use and sold it to private investors.
It was officially restored to the couple's great grandsons, Marcus and Derrick Bruce, on July 20, 2022. The effort involved more than 1,000 hours of pro bono work.

Minow U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Newton_N._Minow)___ was chair of the Federal Communications Commission when he gave a speech, ___E:Television and the Public Interest U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Television_and_the_Public_Interest)___ , describing 1950s television as "a vast wasteland." He later joined Sidley, then Sidley Austin, as a senior counsel.

Former associate ___E:Mike Lee U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Lee)___ (1999-2002),  now a US senator, was the subject of an article entitled, ' Proof morons pass the bar': GOP senator mocked for lawsuit threat against Stephen King. The article referred to a post Lee made following the ___E:assassination of Charlie Kirk U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Assassination_of_Charlie_Kirk)___ suggesting that the Kirk estate sue novelist Stephen King over a comment he made in the wake of the murder.
